mainTopic: Redeeming a פטר חמור, the משנה's list of which מצוה comes first, and how ownership of an animal passes between a Jew and a נכרי for בכורה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question about when you redeem a פטר חמור: right away, or after thirty days. רב ששת says the thirty days is only when delay becomes a sin. רמי בר חמא's ברייתא does not fit that answer, so רבא says the two ברייתות follow רבי אליעזר, who compares the donkey to a firstborn son, and the רבנן, who do not. The משנה then teaches that an owner who will not redeem the donkey breaks its neck. It lists cases where one מצוה comes first: פדיה before עריפה, יעידה before פדיה, יבום before חליצה (later reversed), and the owner's own redemption of הקדש before anyone else's. The פרק ends, and a new משנה teaches that any share a נכרי has in an animal exempts its firstborn from בכורה, while כהנים and לוים are still obligated. The גמרא explains why the מסכת began with the donkey. Then it brings רבי אושעיא's rule that money alone transfers an animal between a Jew and a נכרי. אביי shows from 'מיד עמיתך' that buying from a גוי is done with money. The גמרא then begins the same analysis for a גוי buying from a Jew, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב ששת: thirty days is only when you start transgressing
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת settles the clash between the two ברייתות. The מצוה starts right away, but until thirty days pass you have not done anything wrong by waiting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: The thirty days comes to teach that until then, one does not transgress by not redeeming it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the contradiction on the previous amud. One ברייתא said redeem right away, and the other said after thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He says both are true at different levels. The מצוה of פדיה applies from birth, but there is no עבירה for delaying until the thirty days are up. After that, delaying becomes a transgression.

keyTerms.meaning: a firstborn male donkey, which must be redeemed with a lamb
he transgresses on it, meaning he breaks a prohibition by not acting
thirty days

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It comes to say that he does not transgress on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹבֵר עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between two ברייתות raised on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two sources into two levels: when the מצוה starts, and when delaying becomes a transgression.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות disagree about when the מצוה of redemption begins.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מצוה begins immediately, and one only transgresses after thirty days.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: a ברייתא sounds like you should wait thirty days
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא brings a ברייתא that seems to say the מצוה is to hold off for thirty days, not to redeem right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא objected: 'Its מצוה is all thirty days; from then on, either he redeems it or breaks its neck.' Does this not mean it is a מצוה to keep it, unredeemed, for all thirty days?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא challenges רב ששת. He quotes a ברייתא and reads it as saying the מצוה is to wait the full thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מצוה is to wait thirty days, then the מצוה does not start at birth, and רב ששת is wrong. The words 'from then on, redeem it or break its neck' make it sound like the action only begins after thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: he breaks its neck from behind
does it not mean...? (the opening of a suggested reading)
to keep it waiting, to delay

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama raised an objection:
Its מצוה is all thirty days;
from here onward —
either he redeems it or he breaks its neck.
What, is it not that it is a מצוה
to hold it back for all thirty days?
phrases.notes: He means keeping the donkey without redeeming it until the thirty days are over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's answer from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the מצוה of פדיה starts immediately.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא seems to say the מצוה is to wait thirty days, so the מצוה cannot start at birth.

steps.title: No, the מצוה is to redeem it during the thirty days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רב ששת by reading the ברייתא differently. The thirty days is the time window for redeeming, not a waiting period.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means it is a מצוה to redeem it any time during the thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רמי בר חמא by rereading the ברייתא so that it matches רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Its מצוה is all thirty days' means you may do the מצוה anywhere inside that window, starting from birth. That fits רב ששת exactly: the מצוה starts right away, and the deadline is thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: to redeem it
no, introducing a different reading

phrases.english: No, it is a מצוה to redeem it
throughout the thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, מִצְוָה לִפְדּוֹתוֹ כׇּל שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רמי בר חמא's reading of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the source: the thirty days is a window for doing the מצוה, not a waiting period.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא requires waiting thirty days before redeeming.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא allows redeeming at any point within thirty days, in line with רב ששת.

steps.title: Then the ברייתא should have said 'or he transgresses'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if the thirty days were a deadline, the ברייתא should have said that after it you transgress, not that you break the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should have said: 'From then on, either he redeems it or he transgresses on it!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the defense it just gave by pointing to the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב ששת, what changes after thirty days is that you start sinning. But the ברייתא says that after thirty days you 'redeem it or break its neck.' That sounds like the time when you actually act, not the time when you start sinning.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
it should have said

phrases.english: If so,
'from here onward, either he redeems it'
'or he transgresses on it'
it should have said!
phrases.notes: The ברייתא actually says 'or breaks its neck.' The גמרא is showing how it would read if רב ששת were right.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ אוֹ פּוֹדֵהוּ אוֹ עוֹבֵר עָלָיו מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the defense in step 3 does not fit the ברייתא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 3, and with it רב ששת's approach.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A deadline-based reading would require the wording 'or he transgresses,' but the ברייתא says 'or breaks its neck.'

steps.title: רבא: the two ברייתות follow two different views
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops רב ששת's approach. He says the two ברייתות reflect a real disagreement: רבי אליעזר compares a donkey to a firstborn son, and the רבנן do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: It is not difficult. This one follows רבי אליעזר, who compares the two; that one follows the Rabbis, who do not compare them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a brand-new answer to the original contradiction. Each ברייתא follows a different opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר makes a היקש between פטר חמור and בכור אדם, and a son is redeemed at one month, so for him the donkey is redeemed at thirty days. The רבנן make no such comparison, so for them the donkey is redeemed immediately. There is no need to reinterpret either ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, setting aside the previous approach
it is not difficult; the contradiction can be resolved
compares one law to another (makes a היקש)
the Sages, the majority view

steps.whatToRemember: The question 'immediately or after thirty days?' is a real disagreement. רבי אליעזר compares the donkey to a firstborn son, so he says thirty days. The רבנן do not compare them, so they say immediately.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אלא' means רבא is not adding to רב ששת. He is replacing that answer with a completely different one.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It is not difficult;
this one is Rabbi Eliezer, who compares,
phrases.notes: This is the thirty-days ברייתא. He compares the donkey to a firstborn son, who is redeemed from one month old.

phrases.english: that one is the Rabbis, who do not compare.
phrases.notes: This is the 'right away' ברייתא. Without the comparison, there is no reason to wait.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב ששת's approach runs into trouble in step 4, רבא answers the original contradiction in a new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes each ברייתא to a different תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות must be reconciled within one view, as רב ששת tried.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתות reflect a real disagreement about whether to compare פטר חמור to בכור אדם.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Thirty days follows רבי אליעזר's היקש. Immediately follows the רבנן.

steps.title: משנה: if he won't redeem it, he breaks its neck, but redeeming comes first
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that an owner who does not redeem the פטר חמור must break its neck and bury it. Redemption is still the preferred מצוה, based on the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If he did not want to redeem it, he breaks its neck from behind and buries it. The מצוה of redemption comes before the מצוה of breaking the neck, as it says: 'If you do not redeem it, then you shall break its neck.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives the rule for an owner who does not redeem: עריפה and burial. It also says which מצוה comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'if you do not redeem it, then break its neck.' The words 'if not' show that breaking the neck is only the fallback. So פדיה takes priority over עריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
breaking the neck
he buries it
comes first, takes priority
redemption

steps.whyThisMatters: It opens the משנה's list of priorities that continues in the next steps. Redeeming is the main מצוה, and breaking the neck is only the backup.

phrases.english: משנה: If he did not want to redeem it —
he breaks its neck from behind and buries it.
The מצוה of redemption comes before
the מצוה of breaking the neck,
as it is said:
'If you will not redeem it, then you shall break its neck.'
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from שמות, chapter 13. 'If not' shows that breaking the neck is only the backup plan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An owner who does not redeem a פטר חמור breaks its neck from behind and buries it, and פדיה takes priority over עריפה.

steps.title: Designating a maidservant comes before redeeming her
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that for an אמה עברייה, the master's יעידה comes before letting her go free through פדיה, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה of יעידה comes before the מצוה of פדיה, as the פסוק says: 'who has not designated her, then he shall let her be redeemed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing מצוות where one option comes first. Here it says that marrying the אמה עברייה through יעידה is better than having her redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first mentions 'לא יעדה' (he did not designate her) and only afterward 'והפדה' (let her be redeemed). So פדיה is what happens when יעידה did not happen, which shows that יעידה is the first choice. This follows the same pattern as step 6, where פדיה came before עריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The master (or his son) designating the Hebrew maidservant to become his wife
Redeeming her, paying so she goes free
A Jewish girl sold as a maidservant
Comes first, takes priority

phrases.english: The מצוה of designating comes first
phrases.notes: This is about an אמה עברייה. The master can make her his wife (or his son's wife).

phrases.english: before the מצוה of redeeming
as it says: "who has not designated her, then he shall let her be redeemed."
phrases.notes: שמות כא:ח

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of 'this מצוה comes before that one,' which began with פדיה before עריפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For an אמה עברייה, יעידה takes priority over פדיה.

steps.title: יבום versus חליצה, and how the order changed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says יבום originally came before חליצה. Now that people no longer do יבום for the sake of the מצוה, the חכמים said חליצה comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה of יבום comes before the מצוה of חליצה. That was in earlier times, when people did it for the sake of the מצוה. Now that people do not do it for the sake of the מצוה, the חכמים said the מצוה of חליצה comes before the מצוה of יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another 'which comes first' case: יבום or חליצה. Then it explains that the answer changed over time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the תורה's order, יבום is the main מצוה and חליצה is the fallback. But יבום is only proper when it is done for the sake of the מצוה. Once people started marrying the יבמה for other reasons, the חכמים flipped the order and made חליצה the first choice.

keyTerms.meaning: Marrying the widow of a brother who died without children
The ceremony that releases the widow from יבום
For the sake of the מצוה, with pure intent
In earlier times, originally

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה is saying יבום stopped being a real מצוה. It is still a מצוה. The חכמים only changed which option comes first, because people's intentions changed.

phrases.english: The מצוה of levirate marriage comes first
before the מצוה of chalitza
That was in earlier times, when people would intend
for the sake of the מצוה
but now that they do not intend
for the sake of the מצוה
they said: the מצוה of chalitza comes first
phrases.notes: "They" means the חכמים.

phrases.english: before the מצוה of levirate marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another item in the same list. This one adds the idea that the חכמים reversed the order.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a rule about which option comes first can depend on whether the main option is still done with proper intent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Originally יבום came before חליצה. Now the חכמים say חליצה comes first, because people no longer do יבום for the sake of the מצוה.

steps.title: The owner gets first right to redeem his consecrated animal
steps.stepSummary: When a non-kosher animal is given to הקדש, the original owner has the first right to redeem it, before any other person. This is learned from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה of redemption belongs to the owner. He comes before any other person, as the פסוק says: 'And if it is not redeemed, it shall be sold according to your valuation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the last 'which comes first' case: who should redeem a consecrated non-kosher animal. The answer is the owner, before anyone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that only if it is not redeemed is it sold to others. That means the first option is for the owner to redeem it, and selling it to someone else is the fallback.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption, buying something back from הקדש
Here, the owner who gave the animal to הקדש
Property belonging to the בית המקדש
According to your valuation, at its set price

steps.whatToRemember: The whole list follows one pattern. In each case, the תורה (or the חכמים) makes one option the first choice and the other the fallback: פדיה before עריפה, יעידה before פדיה, יבום before חליצה (later reversed), and the owner before anyone else.

phrases.english: The מצוה of redemption is with the owner
phrases.notes: This is about a non-kosher animal the owner gave to הקדש.

phrases.english: he comes before any other person
as it says: "And if it is not redeemed
phrases.notes: ויקרא כז:כז

phrases.english: it shall be sold according to your valuation."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִצְוַת הַגְּאוּלָּה בָּאָדוֹן הוּא קוֹדֵם לְכׇל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final item in the משנה's list of priorities.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner who gave the animal to הקדש has the first right to redeem it, before any other person.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter of one who buys the fetus of a donkey
steps.stepSummary: The פרק הלוקח עובר חמורו ends with the traditional הדרן formula.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק הלוקח עובר חמורו.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not a new argument. It is the closing line that marks the end of the פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן is a traditional goodbye to the פרק we just finished. It expresses the hope to come back and learn it again. The next פרק opens with a new משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a פרק)
The name of the פרק: 'One who buys the fetus of a donkey'

phrases.english: We will return to you
"One who buys the fetus of his donkey."
phrases.notes: This is the name of the פרק, taken from its first words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the משנה's final rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק of פטר חמור is complete. It ended with a list of cases where one form of a מצוה takes priority over another.

steps.title: New chapter: shared ownership with a non-Jew exempts from firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists five cases where a נכרי has a share in the cow or its fetus. In all of them the firstborn is exempt from בכורה, because the פסוק says "בישראל."
steps.simpleTranslation: If a Jew buys the unborn calf of a non-Jew's cow, or sells his own cow's unborn calf to a non-Jew (even though that sale is not allowed), or becomes partners with a non-Jew, or takes a non-Jew's animal to raise, or gives his own animal to a non-Jew to raise, the calf is exempt from בכורה. The פסוק says "in Israel," and not in others.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new פרק opens with a משנה that lists ways a נכרי can share ownership of an animal. If he has any share, the firstborn has no קדושת בכורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that בכורה only applies when the animal belongs fully to a Jew. Even a partial share held by a נכרי, through partnership or a raising arrangement, removes the obligation. The source is the word "בישראל." The phrase "אף על פי שאינו רשאי" teaches that a forbidden sale still works to exempt the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: A fetus; an unborn animal still inside its mother.
A non-Jew.
One who forms a partnership in owning something.
An arrangement where one person raises another person's animal and they share the profits.
The holiness and obligation of a firstborn animal, which is given to a כהן.

steps.confusionAlert: "פרתו" here means the cow belonging to the נכרי, not to the Jewish buyer.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole פרק: בכורה depends on the animal being fully Jewish-owned.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הַלּוֹקֵחַ עוּבַּר פָּרָתוֹ שֶׁל נׇכְרִי
phrases.english: MISHNA: One who buys the fetus of the cow of a non-Jew
phrases.notes: "His cow" means the non-Jew's cow. The Jew is buying only the unborn calf.

phrases.english: and one who sells to him
phrases.notes: Here a Jew sells the unborn calf of his own cow to a non-Jew.

phrases.english: even though he is not permitted to do so
and one who becomes partners with him
and one who takes an animal from him to raise
and one who gives him an animal to raise
is exempt from the firstborn obligation

phrases.notes: This is from the פסוק "כל בכור בישראל": every firstborn in Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַלּוֹקֵחַ עוּבַּר פָּרָתוֹ שֶׁל נׇכְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק right after the Hadran in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any share a נכרי has in the mother or the fetus exempts the firstborn from בכורה, based on "בישראל."

steps.title: Priests and Levites must give the firstborn of a kosher animal
steps.stepSummary: כהנים and לוים are obligated in בכור בהמה טהורה. They were exempted only from פדיון הבן and פטר חמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: כהנים and לוים are obligated. They were never exempted from the firstborn of a kosher animal. They were exempted only from redeeming a firstborn son and from redeeming a firstborn donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second rule: unlike a נכרי, כהנים and לוים do have בכורה in their kosher animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think that people exempt from some firstborn laws are exempt from all of them. The משנה limits their exemption to two specific laws: redeeming a son and redeeming a donkey. The firstborn of a kosher animal still has full קדושה when they own it.

keyTerms.meaning: Priests and Levites.
A kosher animal, such as a cow, sheep or goat.
Redeeming a firstborn son from a כהן.

steps.whatToRemember: A נכרי's share exempts the animal, but a כהן or a לוי owner does not. They are exempt only from פדיון הבן and פטר חמור.

phrases.english: The priests and the Levites are obligated
for they were not exempted from the firstborn of a kosher animal
but only from redeeming the son and from the firstborn donkey

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a second ruling about who is obligated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים and לוים are obligated in בכור בהמה טהורה. They are exempt only from פדיון הבן and פטר חמור.

steps.title: Why did the tractate start with the donkey instead of the cow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the מסכת opened with פטר חמור, which has only קדושת דמים, before the kosher firstborn, which has the stronger קדושת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did the תנא first teach about the fetus of a donkey and only afterward about the fetus of a cow? He should first teach about the cow's fetus, which has holiness of its body, and then teach about the donkey's fetus, which has holiness only in its value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the order of the פרקים. The first פרק was about the donkey, and only now does this פרק turn to the cow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is that the holier subject should come first. A kosher firstborn has קדושת הגוף: the animal itself is holy and goes on the מזבח. A firstborn donkey has only קדושת דמים: it can be redeemed with a lamb. So the expected order is cow first, donkey second.

keyTerms.meaning: "Why specifically this?" A question about why something was chosen.
First; at the beginning.
Holiness that rests on the body of the animal itself, so it cannot be redeemed.
Holiness that rests only on the animal's money value, so it can be redeemed.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why specifically
does he teach the fetus of his donkey first
and then teach the fetus of his cow?
Let him first teach the fetus of his cow
since it has holiness of the body
and then let him teach the fetus of his donkey
since it has holiness only in its value

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא דְּתָנֵי עוּבַּר חֲמוֹרוֹ בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the opening of the new פרק to question the order of the whole מסכת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the פרקים in מסכת בכורות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The holier subject (קדושת הגוף) should come before the less holy one (קדושת דמים), yet the מסכת does the reverse.

steps.title: First answer: the donkey is dear to the תנא
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of ארץ ישראל answer that the donkey came first because it is dear, following רבי חנינא's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said in the West: if you want, say that since the donkey is dear to him, it comes first, as רבי חנינא taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer: the תנא put the donkey first out of fondness for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא taught earlier in the מסכת that the donkeys helped the Jews leave מצרים by carrying their silver and gold. That special role makes the donkey "beloved," so the תנא honored it by teaching it first, even though its holiness is weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: "In the West," meaning the scholars of ארץ ישראל.
"If you wish, say," which introduces one of two possible answers.
Dear; beloved.

phrases.english: They said in the West
phrases.notes: "The West" means the scholars in ארץ ישראל, which lies west of בבל.

phrases.english: If you wish, say
since it is dear to him
in line with the teaching of רבי חנינא
phrases.notes: רבי חנינא taught earlier in the מסכת that donkeys carried the Jews' silver and gold out of מצרים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the order of the פרקים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the order, based on fondness rather than level of holiness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Topics should be ordered by level of holiness.
steps.terutzMaskana: Love for the donkey, because of its role in יציאת מצרים, justifies teaching it first.

steps.title: Second answer: the donkey's laws are few, so finish them first
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the laws of a non-kosher animal are few, so the תנא finished them first and set them aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say that since the laws about a non-kosher animal are few, he finishes them and puts them aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, practical answer to the same question about the order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the reason is not fondness but how to organize the material. A short topic is cleared away first, and then the longer topic of the kosher firstborn can be taught at length. The core question from step 13 is now resolved in two different ways.

keyTerms.meaning: Few; small in number.
A non-kosher animal, such as a donkey.
He finishes it and casts it aside.

steps.whatToRemember: The donkey comes first in בכורות either because it is beloved (רבי חנינא) or because its laws are few, so the תנא finishes them quickly before the longer topic.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say
since the matters of a non-kosher animal are few
he finishes it and puts it aside
phrases.notes: Literally, "he cuts it off and throws it." He means the short topic is wrapped up first.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא אַיְּידֵי דְּזוּטְרָן מִילֵּיהּ דִּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the same question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: An organizational reason: a short topic is completed first.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Topics should be ordered by level of holiness.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the laws of a non-kosher animal are few, the תנא clears them away first.

steps.title: Buying from a gentile with money alone
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר נחמני, quoting ריש לקיש in the name of רבי אושעיא, rules that money alone transfers ownership of an animal between a Jew and a נכרי "בדיניהם." This decides whether the firstborn is obligated in בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Jew who paid a נכרי for his animal according to their laws owns it even without pulling it, so its firstborn is obligated in בכורה. A נכרי who paid a Jew for his animal according to their laws owns it even without pulling it, so its firstborn is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule: when a Jew and a נכרי buy an animal from each other, paying money is enough to make the sale final.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a Jew buys movable property from another Jew only by pulling it (משיכה), not by paying. Here, when a נכרי is involved, money alone works "בדיניהם." Whoever ends up owning the animal decides the בכורה: a Jewish owner means obligated, and a נכרי owner means exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Money / coins paid for the purchase
Pulled the animal, the usual way to buy movable things
"According to their laws". The meaning is unclear, and the גמרא will ask about it
He acquired it, the sale is final

steps.confusionAlert: Both halves give the same rule about buying (money works). Only the בכורה result flips, because it depends on who owns the animal, a Jew or a נכרי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It links the business laws of buying to the obligation of בכורה. This continues the theme from the משנה that a נכרי's ownership exempts the animal ("בישראל").

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya:
A Jew who gave money to a gentile
for his animal, according to their laws,
phrases.notes: "His animal" means the gentile's animal, which the Jew is buying.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא מָשַׁךְ — קָנָה,
phrases.english: even though he did not pull it, he has acquired it,
and it is obligated in the firstborn law.
And a gentile who gave money to a Jew
for his animal, according to their laws,
phrases.notes: Now it is the Jew's animal, which the gentile is buying.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא מָשַׁךְ — קָנָה,
phrases.english: even though he did not pull it, he has acquired it,
and it is exempt from the firstborn law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the order of the מסכת back to the משנה's topic of a נכרי's share in an animal. It adds the question of how ownership passes between a Jew and a נכרי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Between a Jew and a נכרי, money alone "בדיניהם" transfers ownership of an animal. The firstborn's status follows whoever now owns it.

steps.title: What does "according to their laws" mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first half of the rule again and asks what the word "בדיניהם" refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: a Jew who paid a נכרי according to their laws acquires it even without pulling, and it is obligated in בכורה. What does "according to their laws" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the first half of the rule so it can examine it, and asks what "בדיניהם" means. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא tries out an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Their laws" could mean different things: the laws for buying a נכרי himself, or the way נכרים normally buy and sell property. The גמרא needs to know which one, because that tells us where the rule comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: What? It asks for the meaning of a word

phrases.english: The Master said:
A Jew who gave money to a gentile according to their laws,
even though he did not pull it,
has acquired it, and it is obligated in the firstborn law.
What does "according to their laws" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the רבי אושעיא rule from step 16 and asks about one key word in it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which "laws" the word "בדיניהם" refers to, and so what the source of the rule is.

steps.title: First try: a gentile's body can be bought with money, so surely his property can
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that "בדיניהם" means the laws of buying a נכרי himself as a slave. From there it builds a קל וחומר: if a slave is bought with money, his property surely can be too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say it means the laws of buying his body, the rule would come from a קל וחומר. A Jew can buy a נכרי himself with money, as it says "לרשת אחוזה". The פסוק compares a slave to land: land can be bought with money, a document, or taking possession, so a עבד כנעני can be bought with money. Then surely his property can be bought with money too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible meaning of "בדיניהם": the rules for buying a נכרי as a slave. It shows how a קל וחומר would then teach that his animal is bought with money. This is only a first try, and the גמרא is setting it up to be checked next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "לרשת אחוזה" links a slave to land (a היקש), and land can be bought with money. So a עבד כנעני can be bought with money. If the person himself can be bought with money, then his things, which are a smaller matter, should surely be bought with money as well.

keyTerms.meaning: His body, meaning the person himself bought as a slave
Reasoning from a stronger case to a weaker one
The פסוק compared it, a היקש linking two things
An inherited possession, meaning land
A non-Jewish slave
His property or possessions

steps.confusionAlert: "אי נימא" ("if we say") is only a suggestion the גמרא is testing. Don't treat this קל וחומר as the final answer.

phrases.english: If we say it means according to the laws of his body,
phrases.notes: He means the rules for buying the gentile himself as a slave.

phrases.english: meaning it comes from a kal vachomer:

phrases.aramaic: אִם גּוּפֵיהּ קָנֵי לֵיהּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכֶסֶף,
phrases.english: if a Jew acquires his body with money,
as it is written: "to inherit as a possession,"
phrases.notes: This פסוק is in ויקרא 25, where the Torah talks about owning non-Jewish slaves.

phrases.english: the verse compared him to an ancestral possession (land),
just as land is acquired with money
and with a document and by taking possession,
so too a Canaanite slave is acquired with money.
His property, isn't it all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first possible answer to the question of step 17 and shows the reasoning (קל וחומר plus היקש) behind it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A proposed answer: "בדיניהם" means the laws of buying a נכרי's body. Since his body is bought with money (from the היקש to land), his property is surely bought with money too. The גמרא is about to test this.

steps.title: If the slave comparison works, a document and חזקה should work too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the slave-based קל וחומר. A non-Jewish slave can also be acquired with a שטר or with חזקה, so property should be acquirable those ways as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even with a document and with taking possession it should also work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from Step 18, which said 'בדיניהם' means the laws of buying a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we learn a נכרי's property from how we buy the נכרי himself, we should copy every method of buying a slave. Through the comparison to land, a slave is acquired with money, and also with a שטר or with חזקה. So a נכרי's movable property should also be bought with a שטר or חזקה, and that is not the law.

keyTerms.meaning: A document or deed used to transfer ownership
Taking possession by acting as the owner (for a slave, using his service)
If so (introduces a problematic result of what was just said)

phrases.english: If so,
then even with a document and with taking possession, too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁטָר וּבַחֲזָקָה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר proposed in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'בדיניהם' as the laws of buying a slave, and the קל וחומר built on it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר would carry over every way of buying a slave, including שטר and חזקה, to his property. But movable property is not acquired that way.

steps.title: A Jew buying from a Jew shows the comparison fails
steps.stepSummary: A second problem: a Jewish slave is bought with money, but his property still needs משיכה. So buying the person does not prove how his property is bought.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, a Jew buying from a Jew proves it: his body is bought with money, but his property only with pulling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger attack on the slave-based קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Between two Jews, a person (a Jewish slave) can be bought with money. Yet a Jew's movable property is not acquired with money; it needs משיכה. This proves that 'the body is bought with money' does not lead to 'the property is bought with money.'

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove (a counter-example that breaks a קל וחומר)
His body, meaning the person himself
His property or possessions
Pulling: acquiring an item by drawing it toward yourself
And furthermore (introduces an extra problem)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'body' and 'property' here. Paying money works for buying the person, but it does not work for buying a Jew's things. That gap is exactly what breaks the קל וחומר.

phrases.english: And furthermore, a Jew buying from a Jew will prove it,
phrases.notes: The extra ו at the end looks like a slip; just read it as יוכיח, 'will prove.'

phrases.english: for he acquires his body with money,
phrases.notes: This is a Jewish slave, who is bought with money.

phrases.english: yet his property only with pulling!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent objection to the same קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר: 'if his body is bought with money, surely his property is'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counter-example: between Jews, the body is bought with money but the property is not. So the logic does not hold.

steps.title: אביי: 'their laws' means the laws the Torah set in 'או קנה מיד עמיתך'
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a new meaning of 'בדיניהם'. The פסוק says משיכה applies when buying from your fellow Jew, which implies that buying from a גוי is done with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: 'their laws' means the laws the Torah set for them: 'Or buy from the hand of your fellow.' From your fellow, it is with pulling; but from a גוי, it is with money.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the slave reading was knocked down, אביי gives a fresh answer to Step 17's question about what 'בדיניהם' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'מיד עמיתך' (from your fellow) limits משיכה to deals between Jews. So for a גוי a different method applies, and that method is money. Now the source is a פסוק, not a קל וחומר from slaves.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Or buy from the hand of your fellow' (ויקרא כה:יד)
Your fellow, meaning a fellow Jew
Set or ruled (what the Torah decided)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's source: 'מיד עמיתך' teaches משיכה between Jews, and money when buying from a גוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the base that the rest of this passage tests and defends.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
'Their laws' means the laws that the Torah set for them,
'Or buy from the hand of your fellow' —
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in ויקרא about buying and selling.

phrases.english: it is from the hand of your fellow that it is by pulling,
which implies that from the hand of a gentile it is with money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected slave-based reading with a reading based on a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Torah's laws in 'או קנה מיד עמיתך': משיכה from a Jew, money from a גוי.

steps.title: Maybe you cannot buy from a גוי at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a different reading of the limit: perhaps 'from your fellow' means there is no way at all to buy from a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: from the hand of a gentile, there is no acquisition at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests אביי's reading by offering another way the limit in the פסוק could be read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the limit 'from your fellow' points to money for a גוי. But the limit could just as easily mean that none of the buying methods work with a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (offers another possible reading)
At all

phrases.english: But say: from the hand of a gentile —
there is no acquisition at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: מִיַּד גּוֹי כְּלָל כְּלָל לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what אביי inferred from the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's inference that buying from a גוי is done with money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The limiting word could exclude a גוי completely, instead of switching the method to money.

steps.title: A קל וחומר: if you can buy the person, surely you can buy his property
steps.stepSummary: The answer: it is unthinkable that you cannot buy from a גוי at all. If his very person can be bought, his property certainly can.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: That can't enter your mind. It is a קל וחומר: if his body can be acquired, all the more so his property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the 'no buying at all' reading using simple logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the קל וחומר is used only to show that some way of buying from a גוי must exist. It does not decide which method is used; the פסוק still does that.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind (that idea is impossible)
An argument from a weaker case to a stronger one
All the more so

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same use as the rejected קל וחומר in Step 18. Here it only proves that buying is possible, not which method works.

phrases.english: They said: That cannot enter your mind,
it is a קל וחומר —

phrases.aramaic: אִם גּוּפוֹ קוֹנֶה, מָמוֹנוֹ לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?
phrases.english: if one acquires his body, then his property, all the more so!
phrases.notes: Literally 'his body acquires'; he means a Jew can buy the גוי himself as a slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical קל וחומר that rules out the alternative reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The limit 'from your fellow' might mean you cannot buy from a גוי at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since a גוי's person can be bought, his property surely can be bought.

steps.title: Maybe a גוי's property needs both methods
steps.stepSummary: Another suggestion: perhaps buying from a גוי requires both משיכה and money together.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: from the hand of a gentile, not until there are both!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another possible reading of the פסוק to test אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe 'from your fellow' means משיכה alone is enough only with a Jew. With a גוי you would need money added on top, so two acts.

keyTerms.meaning: Two (both methods together)
Not until there is

phrases.english: But say: from the hand of a gentile —
not until there are two!
phrases.notes: The two are pulling and paying money, both done together.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: מִיַּד גּוֹי עַד דְּאִיכָּא תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to אביי's inference after the first one was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that money alone works with a גוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The limit could mean that buying from a גוי needs more, not a different method.

steps.title: The person needs one act, so his property can't need two
steps.stepSummary: The answer uses a קל וחומר again: the גוי himself is bought with one act, so his property cannot need two.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Isn't it a קל וחומר? His body with one, and his property with two?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the 'both methods' idea with logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Buying a person is the more serious purchase, and it takes only one act. It would make no sense for his property to be harder to buy than he is.

keyTerms.meaning: And isn't it? (asked to show the answer is obvious)
With one (act)
With two (acts)

phrases.english: They said: Isn't it a קל וחומר?
His body with one act, and his property with two?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 24's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Buying from a גוי might need both משיכה and money.
steps.terutzMaskana: Property cannot be harder to buy than the person, so one act is enough.

steps.title: Maybe either method works with a גוי
steps.stepSummary: A third suggestion: perhaps with a גוי you can buy with either משיכה or money.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: either with this or with that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers one more reading that would weaken אביי's 'money only' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since one act is enough, maybe both acts are allowed as options. That would fit the קל וחומר, yet it would not limit a גוי to money.

keyTerms.meaning: Either with this or with that (either method works)

phrases.english: But say: either with this or with that,
phrases.notes: 'This' and 'that' are pulling and money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After 'two acts' is rejected, this suggests that either single act works.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that money is the method with a גוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both one-act options would fit the logic, so why restrict a גוי to money?

steps.title: It must be like 'your fellow': one set method
steps.stepSummary: The answer begins: the law for a גוי must match the law for 'your fellow.' Just as with a Jew there is one set method, with a גוי there is also one set method, which is money.
steps.simpleTranslation: It must be similar to 'your fellow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the 'either one' idea. The next step finishes the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule for a גוי is learned by contrast with 'your fellow,' so it should follow the same pattern. A Jew has one fixed method (משיכה), so a גוי also has one fixed method (money), not a choice.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, matching the pattern of

steps.whatToRemember: The final conclusion: buying from a גוי is done with one act, money. This matches the single act (משיכה) used between Jews.

phrases.english: Similar to 'your fellow.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 26's 'either one' suggestion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Matching the pattern of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either משיכה or money might work with a גוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Like 'your fellow,' who has one method, a גוי also has one method: money.

steps.title: Buying from a Jew takes one method, so buying from a non-Jew does too
steps.stepSummary: The answer from step 27 is completed. Buying from 'your fellow' takes one method (משיכה), so buying from a גוי also takes only one method (money).
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as buying from 'your fellow' is done with one method, so too buying from a non-Jew is done with one method.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer it started in step 27. Buying from a גוי, like buying from a Jew, uses only one method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion in step 26 was that a Jew could buy from a גוי with either משיכה or money. The answer is that the פסוק sets up a parallel. Buying from 'your fellow' has one fixed method (משיכה), so buying from a גוי must also have one fixed method, and that method is money.

keyTerms.meaning: Your fellow, meaning another Jew (from the פסוק).
With one, meaning with a single method of acquiring.
So too ... also. This makes a parallel between two cases.

steps.whatToRemember: When a Jew buys from a גוי, there is exactly one method, and that method is money. The גמרא now turns to the reverse case, a גוי buying from a Jew.

phrases.english: Just as 'your fellow' is with one [method],
so too a non-Jew is also with one [method].

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה ״עֲמִיתֶךָ״ בַּחֲדָא, אַף גּוֹי נָמֵי בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel drawn from the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Buying from a גוי might work with either משיכה or money.
steps.terutzMaskana: Buying from a גוי, like buying from a Jew, uses one single method: money.

steps.title: A non-Jew who pays money for a Jew's animal acquires it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the second half of רבי אושעיא's ruling from step 16: a גוי who paid a Jew for his animal 'according to their laws' acquires it even without pulling it, and the animal is exempt from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: A non-Jew who gave money to a Jew for his animal, according to their laws, acquires it even though he did not pull it, and it is exempt from the law of the firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the source it is studying and quotes its next ruling, so that it can explain it. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps dealt with a Jew buying from a גוי. Now the case is reversed: a גוי buys from a Jew. Paying money alone is enough for the גוי to own the animal. Since the animal now belongs to a non-Jew, its firstborn does not get the holiness of בכורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Money, coins.
He pulled. Pulling an item is a way of acquiring it.
The law of the firstborn animal, which is given to a כהן.

phrases.english: The Master said:
And a non-Jew who gave money to a Jew
for his animal, according to their laws,
phrases.notes: 'His animal' means the Jew's animal, which the non-Jew is buying.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא מָשַׁךְ — קָנָה,
phrases.english: even though he did not pull it, he acquired it,
and it is exempt from the firstborn law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: וְגוֹי שֶׁנָּתַן מָעוֹת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בִּבְהֶמְתּוֹ בְּדִינֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second clause of רבי אושעיא's ruling (step 16), the reverse case of the previous discussion: a גוי buying from a Jew.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי who pays a Jew for his animal acquires it with money alone, without pulling it, and the animal is exempt from בכורה.

steps.title: What does 'according to their laws' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase 'according to their laws' refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'according to their laws' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about one phrase in the ruling it just quoted. The next steps will try to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'their laws' is unclear. It could mean the way a גוי buys a person, or some other rule. The answer will show where the rule that a גוי buys with money comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: What? This is a question word asking for the meaning of something.
According to their laws, meaning the rules of acquiring that apply to non-Jews.
A law or rule.

phrases.english: What is 'according to their laws'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in the ruling quoted in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'their laws' are, and where the rule that a גוי acquires with money comes from.

steps.title: First suggestion: learn it from how a non-Jew buys a Jewish person
steps.stepSummary: Maybe 'their laws' refers to how a גוי buys a Jew's body, which is with money. By a קל וחומר, he should be able to buy the Jew's property with money too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means their laws for buying a person: we can learn it with a קל וחומר. If a non-Jew can buy a Jew's body with money, as the פסוק says 'from the money of his purchase,' then surely he can buy the Jew's property with money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible answer. It says the rule comes from how a גוי buys a Jewish slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah shows that a גוי buys a Jewish slave with money. The argument says that a person is a 'bigger' thing to acquire than property. So if money works for the person, it should surely work for his property too.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. This introduces a suggestion that may be rejected.
His body, meaning the person himself, bought as a slave.
A 'how much more so' argument, reasoning from a stronger case to a weaker one.
His property or possessions.
All the more so.

phrases.english: If you say: 'according to their laws' for the body,
phrases.notes: He means the way a non-Jew buys a Jew as a slave.

phrases.english: because it comes through a kal vachomer:

phrases.aramaic: אִם גּוּפוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל קָנֵי לֵיהּ בְּכֶסֶף,
phrases.english: If a Jew's body, [a non-Jew] acquires it with money,
as it is written: 'from the money of his purchase,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא כה

phrases.english: his property, is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question in step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Their laws' means the law of buying a Jewish person with money. By a קל וחומר, his property is bought with money too.

steps.title: Rejected: a Jew buying from a Jew proves otherwise
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר fails. When a Jew buys from a Jew, the person (an עבד עברי) is bought with money, but property is bought only with משיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Jew buying from a Jew proves this wrong: his body is bought with money, but his property only by pulling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the first suggestion. It shows a case where the method for a person and the method for property are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed that whatever method works for a person must work for property. But between two Jews, a Hebrew slave is bought with money while property needs משיכה. So the method of buying a person tells us nothing about the method of buying property.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove. A case brought to show that an argument does not hold.
Money, used here as a method of acquiring.
Pulling an item toward oneself to acquire it.

phrases.english: A Jew [buying] from a Jew will prove [otherwise],
for his body is acquired with money,
yet his property [is acquired only] by pulling!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the קל וחומר suggested in step 31.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the way a person is bought to set the method for buying property.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Between two Jews, a person is bought with money while property needs משיכה. So the method for a person and the method for property do not have to match.

steps.title: אביי: the Torah's own rule, from 'וכי תמכרו ממכר לעמיתך'
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that 'their laws' are the rules the Torah set for non-Jews. The פסוק says selling 'to your fellow' is by pulling, which implies that selling to a גוי is with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: 'their laws' means the laws the Torah set for them. 'And if you sell something to your fellow': to your fellow it is by pulling, which means that to a non-Jew it is with money.
steps.whatsHappening: After the first idea was rejected, אביי gives the real answer. He finds the rule in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'to your fellow' limit משיכה to a sale between Jews. That suggests a sale to a גוי works differently, with money. This is the same פסוק used in the earlier discussion, now applied to a Jew selling to a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah set for them, meaning the rule the Torah fixed for non-Jews.
A sale item, something being sold.
But this one, meaning the opposite case, which we learn by implication.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
'According to their laws' that the Torah set for them,
'And if you sell a sale item to your fellow':
phrases.notes: This is from ויקרא כה, the same פסוק used earlier in the discussion.

phrases.english: to your fellow, by pulling,
but to a non-Jew, with money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בְּדִינֵיהֶם שֶׁפָּסְקָה לָהֶם תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected suggestion of step 31 with a source from a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Their laws' is the Torah's rule from 'וכי תמכרו ממכר לעמיתך': selling to a Jew is by משיכה, and selling to a גוי is with money.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the ruling in step 29 that a גוי acquires a Jew's animal with money alone, which makes it exempt from בכורה.

steps.title: Maybe a non-Jew cannot buy at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי's reading. Perhaps the פסוק means that a גוי cannot buy from a Jew in any way.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: to a non-Jew, not at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests אביי's reading by suggesting another way to read the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'to your fellow' limits משיכה to Jews, the limit might mean that a גוי has no way of buying at all, and not that he buys with money. This challenge copies the one raised earlier in the reverse case.

keyTerms.meaning: But say. This introduces another possible reading that challenges the last one.
Not at all, in no way whatsoever.
To a non-Jew.

phrases.english: But say: to a non-Jew, not at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what אביי learned from the פסוק in step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading that 'to a גוי' means with money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The limiting word 'to your fellow' could just as easily mean a גוי cannot buy at all.

steps.title: If a non-Jew can buy a Jew's body, surely he can buy his property
steps.stepSummary: The answer is a קל וחומר. Since a גוי can buy a Jew himself, he can surely buy his property, so 'not at all' is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Isn't it a קל וחומר? If he can acquire the person himself, can he not all the more so acquire his property?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge. It shows that a גוי must be able to buy a Jew's property somehow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah allows a גוי to buy a Jew as a slave. So it cannot be that he is unable to buy the Jew's property in any way. The קל וחומר proves only that buying is possible, and the פסוק tells us the method is money.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it ...? A question asked to point out the obvious.
Acquired or bought.

steps.confusionAlert: In step 32 a similar קל וחומר was rejected, so why does it work now? There it tried to prove the method (money). Here it only proves that buying is possible at all, and step 32's objection does not touch that point.
steps.whatToRemember: A גוי can buy from a Jew (shown by the קל וחומר), and his method is money (shown by the פסוק).

phrases.english: They said: Is it not a kal vachomer?
If he acquires [a Jew's] body,
his property, is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: קל וחומר showing that buying must be possible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גוי might not be able to buy a Jew's property at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since a גוי can buy a Jew's body, he can surely buy his property. So the פסוק must mean he buys with money.

steps.title: Maybe a non-Jew needs both acts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a גוי only acquires a Jew's property once he does both acts: paying money and pulling.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that for a גוי, the sale is not final until there are two acts (money and pulling)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי again. Maybe the פסוק means a גוי needs both money and משיכה, not money alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 35 ruled out the idea that a גוי can't buy at all. Now the גמרא tries a new reading: a Jew uses one act (משיכה), so maybe a גוי needs one more act on top of that. That would mean money alone is not enough for a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / maybe it means (the גמרא proposing a different reading)
Not until there is
Two (here: both money and משיכה)

phrases.english: Say: for a non-Jew
phrases.notes: He's suggesting another way to read the פסוק from step 33.

phrases.english: not until there are two!
phrases.notes: The 'two' are the two acts: paying money and pulling the item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the 'not at all' reading was rejected, the גמרא offers a different alternative reading of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading that a גוי acquires with money alone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק only says a Jew uses משיכה; it could imply that a גוי needs money plus משיכה, not money instead of משיכה.

steps.title: A קל וחומר rules out needing two acts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a קל וחומר: a גוי buys a Jew's body with one act, so he cannot need two acts to buy the Jew's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a קל וחומר? His body is bought with one act, and his property would need two?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the 'both acts' idea. It would make no sense for property to be harder to buy than the person himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know a גוי buys a Jew as a servant with money alone (one act). Buying property should be easier than buying a person, not harder. So a גוי cannot need two acts for property.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it a קל וחומר? (logic from the stricter case to the easier one)
His body (the Jew himself, sold as a servant)
His property / money

phrases.english: Is it not a קל וחומר?
His body with one act,
phrases.notes: A גוי can buy a Jew's body with money alone, as mentioned in step 31.

phrases.english: and his property with two?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the suggestion of step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: קל וחומר from the stronger case (acquiring the person) to the lighter case (acquiring property).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גוי might need both money and משיכה to buy property.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since one act is enough for the body, one act must be enough for property.

steps.title: Maybe a non-Jew can use either act
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a גוי can acquire property with either money or משיכה, whichever he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that a גוי acquires either with this (pulling) or with that (money).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one more alternative. Maybe a גוי is not limited to money only, and משיכה works for him too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 37 proved a גוי needs only one act. But that does not yet prove which act. Maybe both options work for him, so the פסוק would not be teaching that he uses money only.

keyTerms.meaning: Either with this or with that

phrases.english: But say: either with this
phrases.notes: 'This' means pulling the item (משיכה).

phrases.english: or with that,
phrases.notes: 'That' means paying money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After 'both acts' was rejected, the גמרא proposes the opposite: either act alone works.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that a גוי acquires specifically with money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק limits only the Jew to משיכה; perhaps a גוי is not limited at all and can use either method.

steps.title: It must be like 'your fellow'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: the rule for a גוי must be similar to the rule for 'your fellow', which has one set method.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similar to 'your fellow'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the 'either one' suggestion. This line sets up the answer, and the full explanation continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule for a גוי is learned from the פסוק about 'your fellow' (a Jew), and a Jew has exactly one method: משיכה. So the rule we learn for a גוי should also be one fixed method, which is money, not a free choice between two.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to 'your fellow' (the פסוק about selling to a Jew)

steps.whatToRemember: A גוי needs only one act to acquire a Jew's property (קל וחומר from acquiring his body), and the גמרא is building toward that one act being money, working like 'your fellow', which has one fixed act.

phrases.english: similar to 'your fellow';
phrases.notes: This points back to the פסוק from step 33 about selling 'to your fellow'. The explanation keeps going in the next lines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the 'either act' suggestion of step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to the source case in the פסוק: the rule for a גוי must work like the rule for 'your fellow'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גוי might acquire with either money or משיכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Like 'your fellow', who has one fixed method, a גוי also has one fixed method. The full explanation continues in the next part of the text.
